themes_detail.label: Graffiti Surge in Midwood
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked dramatically to 23 this week, an 820% increase from the 2.5-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting a concentrated tagging campaign or enforcement gap in CD314 this week.
evidence: 23 graffiti complaints this week vs. 2.5-complaint weekly average (8-week baseline)
z-score of 11.84 indicates extreme statistical outlier
820% spike represents most dramatic anomaly in dataset
reporting_angles: Ground canvassing: Map where the 23 complaints are clustered—is it one corridor or dispersed?
Interview NYPD/Sanitation: Why the sudden surge this week? Any known crews or organized tagging?

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Spike (Non-Residential)
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 100 this week, a 292% increase from the 25.5-complaint weekly average, marking a sharp and unexplained escalation in outdoor noise disturbance across the district this week.
evidence: 100 street/sidewalk noise complaints this week vs. 25.5-complaint weekly average (8-week baseline)
z-score of 4.14 indicates highly significant spike
292% increase concentrated in single week with no prior escalation pattern
reporting_angles: Temporal analysis: Is the spike concentrated on certain days/times? Could indicate event, construction, or commercial activity?
Resident interviews: What specific noise sources are residents reporting? Construction, vehicle traffic, street vendors, entertainment venues?

themes_detail.label: Air Quality Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints spiked to 5 this week, a 700% increase from the 0.6-complaint weekly average, suggesting a localized air quality incident or pollution event in Midwood/Ocean Parkway this week.
evidence: 5 air quality complaints this week vs. 0.6-complaint weekly average (8-week baseline)
z-score of 9.04 indicates extremely significant spike
700% increase with virtually no baseline complaints—suggests new source or event
reporting_angles: EPA/DEP air monitoring: Check AirNow or NYC DEP data for particulate/pollution readings in 11218/11219 zip codes this week
Source investigation: Interview complainants about timing and location—could indicate industrial emission, major fire, construction dust, or traffic congestion

themes_detail.label: Elevator Failures Rising
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints reached 5 this week, a 74% increase from the 2.9-complaint weekly average, indicating emerging building maintenance issues affecting residents in residential buildings this week.
evidence: 5 elevator complaints this week vs. 2.9-complaint weekly average (8-week baseline)
z-score of 3.54 indicates statistically significant spike
74% increase concentrated in single week amid broader construction activity (327 DOB permit filings in 90 days)
reporting_angles: Building inspection audit: Cross-reference elevator complaints with DOB violation records for the 5 affected buildings
Maintenance backlog: Are elevator service companies overwhelmed? Interview property managers about inspection delays

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Campaign
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints peaked at 6 complaints two weeks ago, a 1500% spike from the 0.4-complaint weekly average, indicating a possible large-scale poster campaign or enforcement lapse in the district two weeks ago.
evidence: 6 illegal posting complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4-complaint weekly average (8-week baseline)
1500% spike—most extreme percentage increase besides graffiti—suggests coordinated activity
reporting_angles: Visual survey: Walk high-complaint blocks to photograph remaining posted materials and identify subject matter (political, commercial, event promotion)
Sanitation enforcement: Did the city respond to the spike? How quickly were postings removed?
